title: Francesco Grossetti
text:
Short Bio
I am an Assistant Professor of Accounting Analytics and Data Science at the Department of Accounting at Bocconi University, a Fellow at the Bocconi Institute for Data Science and Analytics, and a member of the Bocconi Digital Transformation and AI Committee.
My work sits at the intersection of Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, and empirical finance. I use large-scale textual and multimodal financial data to study corporate disclosure and its consequences — including firm tax outcomes and investor reactions to multi-dimensional financial narratives. Methodologically, I draw on statistical learning and computational statistics, with a focus on stochastic processes for sequential data, which lets me model how corporate information evolves over time (disclosure cascades, topic model identification, and more).
My work has appeared in the Review of Accounting Studies, the Journal of Machine Learning Research, the Journal of Accounting and Public Policy, and other outlets.

Research

My research focuses on how firms communicate with capital markets through text — annual reports, conference calls, codes of conduct, loan contracts, and tax disclosures — and on what investors, regulators, and machine-learning systems can recover from those communications. I combine NLP, statistical learning, and stochastic-process models with empirical accounting and finance, with a particular interest in disclosure cascades, topic-model diagnostics, and the limits of large language models in highly specialized domains.
Recent grants and recognitions:

CIVICA Faculty Short Visits Program (March 2024) — Optimal Benchmarking for Mutual Fund Performance Evaluation with NLP, at IE University.
Bocconi Senior Research Grant, Co-PI (2020–2021, €9,000) — Multi-modal Communication in Corporate Reporting, with A. Caglio.
Bocconi Junior Research Grant, PI (2019–2020, €8,000) — edgartools: An Open Source Library to Efficiently Collect Financial Filings from the SEC EDGAR Database.






Service, Teaching and Outreach

I serve on the Editorial Board of Accounting in Europe (2026–2029) and as Scientific Program Coordinator of the 4th Bocconi Accounting Symposium (June 22–23, 2026). I review for the Journal of Accounting and Public Policy, the Journal of Business, Finance, and Accounting, and the FARS section of AAA.
At Bocconi I have designed and direct courses that bring data science, NLP, and blockchain into the MSc. and BSc. curricula in Accounting and AI. In 2023–2024 I received the Bocconi Teaching Award for Innovation for the course Introduction to Blockchain.
Current courses — Bocconi University:

Big Data for Business Decisions — MSc. Elective
Statistical and Computational Methods in Accounting — BSc. in AI, Elective
Introduction to Blockchain — BSc. Elective · Bocconi Teaching Award for Innovation, 2023–2024

I also teach Introduction to Blockchain at NHH (Bergen) and the Free University of Bozen (2024–2025), and the NLP module of Mastering Data for Insurance at SDA Bocconi Executive Custom Program.
Since 2018 I have advised more than 40 MSc. and 30 BSc. theses on corporate disclosure, NLP, machine learning, and blockchain applications in accounting. Prospective advisees: please email me with a short note on your background and the questions you would like to work on.

title: Francesco Grossetti

Code
I am an active developer of open-source tools for empirical accounting and finance research. All projects live on GitHub.







Reproducibility
Where possible, the code that accompanies my published papers is released alongside the working-paper version. If you are looking for replication materials for a specific paper and cannot find them, please email me.
